title: ephemeral-boot-and-attestation-playbook-for-onprem-deploys-2026
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's recommended operational procedures for building, delivering, and operating ephemeral-boot images for private (on-prem / VPC) deployments with measured boot attestation and secure live-patching. It focuses on reducing blast radius for field operators, minimizing sensitive image exposure, and enabling safe fast path upgrades for model runtime artifacts (weights, quantized kernels, KV cache formats) in environments where full air-gapped, FIPS, or HSM-backed requirements may apply.

Intended audience:
- Field engineers responsible for on-prem installs and upgrades
- SRE and platform engineers running Private control planes
- Security reviewers and compliance owners

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private-deployments using Redwood Private or our operator-managed on-prem packages.
- Target platforms: x86_64 with UEFI secure boot support, select ARM deployments where measured boot telemetry is available.
- Assumes customer has a hardware root-of-trust (TPM 2.0) or equivalent and network connectivity for attestation channel (can be configured to use an offline cassette for fully air-gapped installs).

Goals:
1) Provide a reproducible ephemeral image pipeline where images are: minimal, signed, and have verifiable boot measurements.
2) Enable safe live-patching and model artifact swaps without full host reimaging whenever possible.
3) Define deterministic rollback and isolation steps to recover from failed updates.

Terminology:
- Ephemeral boot image: a read-only OS+runtime artifact that boots a compute node into a known state and mounts model artifacts remotely or from local immutable storage.
- Measured boot: a chain-of-trust measurement (UEFI/TPM PCRs) recorded during boot used for attestation.
- Attestation server: Redwood or customer-side service which verifies measurements against a trusted allowlist.

Prerequisites (checklist):
1) Hardware: TPM 2.0 present or HSM accessible; BIOS/UEFI firmware supports Secure Boot and measured boot PCRs.
2) Network: management plane access between node and attestation endpoint (or pre-seeded attestation cassette).
3) Software: image-builder (Packer/BuildStream), signatures toolchain (cosign or internal sigserver), kexec utility for fast kernel swaps.
4) Keys: signing keys stored in KMS/HSM; only public verification material distributed to operator consoles.

Ephemeral image build and pipeline (recommended flow):
1) Base build: Create minimal OS image with only necessary kernel modules, GPU drivers, container runtime, and Redwood runtime binaries. Remove SSH keys, admin credentials, and cloud agents.
2) Immutable runtime layer: package Redwood runtime and GPU optimizations as a read-only artifact. Validate with unit tests and perf smoke tests.
3) Model artifact packaging: store model binaries and quantized variants as separate, versioned blobs. Do NOT bake large model weights into ephemeral images unless required for air-gapped installs (see Air-gapped section).
4) Sign and attest: generate SBOM, compute image hash, sign image with HSM-backed key (cosign recommended), and produce a signed measurement manifest describing expected UEFI PCR values for the image.
5) Publish to registry/artifact store: push signed artifacts to customer-side registry (or Redwood storage for hybrid installs) and update the attestation allowlist.

Attestation modes:
- Online attestation: node boots, collects PCR values, and POSTs measurement manifest to attestation server. Server verifies signature and returns a short-lived attestation token used to unlock model blob decryption keys.
- Cassette (air-gapped) attestation: pre-compute measurement allowlist and provide cassette (signed token package) to operator to be imported during install. Tokens expire after specified window to enforce rotation.

Boot and runtime verification steps (operator commands):
1) Boot the ephemeral image with secure boot enabled. Check UEFI settings: 'SecureBoot: Enabled', 'BootOrder set to PXE/LOCAL'.
2) Verify measurement: curl -ksS --cert <operator-cert> https://attest.example.com/verify -d '{"node_id":"$(hostname)","pcr_values":"$(tpm2_pcrread)"}'
3) Confirm attestation token present: /opt/redwood/attestation/token.json (expires).
4) Pull model blobs using attestation token: redwoodctl fetch-model --token /opt/redwood/attestation/token.json --model-id m1234

Live-patching and kernel swap strategy (to avoid full reboot):
- When only runtime libraries, inference kernels or quantized weight shims need update, prefer kexec-based kernel+initramfs swaps together with overlayfs model blob updates. This reduces downtime and avoids re-attestation for unchanged PCR measurements if configured carefully.
- Constraints: kexec will change kernel measurement PCRs; include kexec-allowed hashes in attestation allowlist or use attestation server policy to accept approved kexec events.
- Steps for safe kexec-based update:
  1) Stage new kernel and initramfs on /var/lib/redwood/staged/
  2) Run integration smoke-tests against staged runtime in a containerized verifier.
  3) Mark node as "draining" in control-plane and migrate active requests.
  4) Trigger kexec: sudo /usr/sbin/kexec -l /var/lib/redwood/staged/vmlinuz --initrd=/var/lib/redwood/staged/initrd.img --command-line="$(cat /proc/cmdline) redwood.upgrade_token=<token>"
  5) On reboot, node will re-attest. Control-plane verifies token and unmarks node when model pull completes.

Rolling upgrade playbook (operator procedure):
1) Canary: select 2 nodes in each availability stripe. Apply ephemeral image and runtime changes, run full end-to-end eval against canary prompt set (latency, accuracy, throughput).
2) Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 30–60 minute observation windows and automated auto-rollback conditions.
3) Auto-rollback triggers:
  - 99th percentile tail latency increase > 30% vs baseline for 15 minutes
  - Token fetch failures > 2% of requests for 10 minutes
  - Model correctness regression: dropped generation score > configured threshold on regression prompts
4) Manual hold: SRE or release owner can pause rollout in console. Document reason and required remediation steps.

Rollback and failure isolation matrix:
- Failure type: Node boot fails (bootloop) -> Isolation: detach from LB, boot into recovery image, collect TPM/UEFI logs, escalate to firmware vendor if needed.
- Failure type: Model blob decryption fails -> Isolation: revoke attestation token, fallback to cold model variant with local copy, notify security.
- Failure type: kexec failure -> Isolation: auto-fallback to previous kernel via bootloader saved entry; if not present, instruct operator to recover via console and re-image from signed artifact.

Verification and acceptance tests (must pass on every upgrade):
1) Boot measurement validity check (scripted).
2) Attestation handshake round-trip within 5s average latency.
3) Model fetch with token success rate >= 99.9% in staged network.
4) E2E perf: p50 latency within +10% of baseline, p99 under SLA.
5) Regression check: prompt-set accuracy drop < configured threshold (default 1.5% relative).

Air-gapped/fully offline deployment guidance:
- Option A (preferred): pre-seed model blobs and signed attestation cassette. Provide local attestation server appliance that validates PCRs against precomputed allowlist.
- Option B (immutable images): bake model weight bundles into read-only image signed by HSM. Larger image size increases distribution time; ensure checksum verification and storage lifecycle policies.

Telemetry and observability recommendations (day-2):
- Collect boot measurement deltas, attestation result codes, token issuance latencies, model fetch success/failure, and kexec event logs.
- Tag telemetry by tenant_id, node_role, and orchestration_phase. Retention: default 90 days for operational events, 365 days for security-critical attestation events.

Runbook snippets (quick commands):
- Verify signed image: cosign verify --key kms://projects/prod/keys/onprem-signer <image-ref>
- Read TPM PCRs: tpm2_pcrread sha256:0,1,2,3
- Force node into recovery: redwoodctl node set-state --node-id n-12345 --state recovery --reason "boot failure"
- Rotate attestation cassette (air-gapped): redact and sign with operator key: redwoodctl cassette sign --cassette /tmp/cassette.json --key /opt/keys/operator.pem --expire 72h

Ownership and escalation:
- Build & Sign pipeline: Platform Security (owner).
- Field installs / day-2 ops: Private Deployments field-engineering team.
- Attestation server: Security + Infra (joint ownership).
- Escalation path: On-call field-eng -> On-call infra -> Security pager -> Firmware vendor.

Troubleshooting matrix (common symptoms):
- Symptom: Attestation token not granted. Checks: verify cosign signature of image, check TPM PCRs mismatch, inspect attestation server policy logs for mismatches.
- Symptom: Model fetch timeout. Checks: token TTL, network egress rules, registry reachability (tcp/443), token-scoped permissions.
- Symptom: Unexpected reboots after kexec. Checks: kernel command-line parity, signed initrd, bootloader preserved previous entry.

Appendix A — Minimal security checklist (table-style):
- Signed image present: YES
- SBOM attached: YES
- TPM present: YES / NO (action: do not proceed without TPM unless HSM path)
- Attestation path available: ONLINE / CASSETTE
- Recovery image available: YES

Appendix B — Example attestation policy (pseudo YAML):
policy_id: redwood-ephemeral-1
allowed_pcrs:
  - sha256: [<hash-kernel>, <hash-initrd>, <hash-os>]
kexec_policy: require_signed_kexec: true
trusted_keys: ["projects/prod/keys/onprem-signer"]
